effects: The contract defines no such typed message; the only unlink message it verifies is Unlink(handleId,profileId,nonce,deadline), so this format matches no real signature.
The real Unlink signature lets anyone call unlinkWithSig to remove the link between the handle and the Lens profile (handle stops resolving to the profile, profile loses its default handle).
The real signature uses up the signer's current nonce in TokenHandleRegistry and stays valid until its deadline.
formats.shown: A screen titled "unlink_with_sig" with three raw numbers labelled handle_id, profile_id and signatureDeadline, under domain "Lens Protocol Profiles" v2.

findings.title: unlink_with_sig: the primary type and its members do not exist in the verifying contract.
findings.evidence: Typehash.sol: `bytes32 constant UNLINK = keccak256('Unlink(uint256 handleId,uint256 profileId,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)');` TokenHandleRegistry._validateUnlinkSignature hashes only this type. Descriptor key: "unlink_with_sig(uint256 handle_id,uint256 profile_id,uint256 signatureDeadline)" has a different name, different member names and no nonce.
findings.fix: Delete this format. The contract signs only Unlink and Link; describe those with their exact encodeType strings.

findings.title: unlink_with_sig: the EIP-712 domain name and version differ from the ones TokenHandleRegistry uses.
findings.evidence: TokenHandleRegistry.calculateDomainSeparator: `keccak256('TokenHandleRegistry'), EIP712_DOMAIN_VERSION_HASH` with `EIP712_DOMAIN_VERSION = '1'`. Descriptor context.eip712.domain: {"name": "Lens Protocol Profiles", "version": "2"} (the LensHub domain).

findings.title: unlink_with_sig: the intent is a function name and the deadline shows as a raw integer.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "intent": "unlink_with_sig"; field signatureDeadline "format": "raw"; labels handle_id, profile_id are code identifiers.
findings.fix: Use intent "Unlink handle from Lens profile", labels "Handle ID", "Profile ID", and format date with encoding timestamp for the deadline.

findings.title: unlink_with_sig: the only test uses placeholder 1e18 values for every field, under a type the contract lacks.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json message: handle_id, profile_id and signatureDeadline all "1000000000000000000"; primaryType "unlink_with_sig".
findings.fix: Replace with a test of the real Unlink message using a realistic handle id, profile id and deadline.

effects: The signature lets anyone call unlinkWithSig to delete the link between handle handleId and Lens profile profileId: the handle no longer resolves to the profile and the profile loses its default handle.
The signature uses up the signer's current TokenHandleRegistry nonce, which cancels any other pending signature with that nonce.
The signature stays valid until the deadline timestamp.
formats.shown: A screen titled "unlink" with raw handleId, profileId and nonce; the deadline is hidden; domain is set to "Lens Protocol Profiles" v2.

findings.title: unlink: the EIP-712 domain name and version differ from the ones TokenHandleRegistry verifies.
findings.evidence: TokenHandleRegistry.calculateDomainSeparator: `keccak256('TokenHandleRegistry'), EIP712_DOMAIN_VERSION_HASH` with `EIP712_DOMAIN_VERSION = '1'`. Descriptor context.eip712.domain: {"name": "Lens Protocol Profiles", "version": "2"}. A message under the descriptor's domain is not the one the contract accepts, and real Unlink messages never match this descriptor.

findings.title: unlink: the format key uses primary type "unlink", but the contract hashes type "Unlink".
findings.evidence: Typehash.sol: `keccak256('Unlink(uint256 handleId,uint256 profileId,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)')`. Descriptor key: "unlink(uint256 handleId,uint256 profileId,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)". encodeType is case-sensitive, so the type hash differs.
findings.fix: Rename the format key to "Unlink(uint256 handleId,uint256 profileId,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)".

findings.title: unlink: the intent is a bare verb and labels are code identifiers; it does not say what is unlinked.
findings.fix: Use intent "Unlink handle from Lens profile", labels "Handle ID" and "Profile ID", and add an interpolatedIntent "Unlink handle {handleId} from profile {profileId}".

findings.title: unlink: handleId is a token id that stands for the handle name, which the descriptor cannot show.
findings.evidence: TokenHandleRegistry._unlink takes `uint256 handleId` of LENS_HANDLES; the name lives in the LensHandles contract, not in the message. Case 1 shows handleId "904217".
